reading: The few coloured cells in one corner are completed to full 4-fold (D4) symmetry about the grid centre; then the colour sitting two steps from a corner cell along its row/column is drawn as a dotted line (every second cell) between that corner and its mirror images, forming a dotted square frame.

slots.seed: the corner cluster of coloured cells
slots.frame_colour: colour of the cell two steps along the row/column from the corner cell of the frame
slots.frame_ends: the corner cell and its mirror copies
slots.spacing: every second cell between the ends

why: the output is D4-symmetric and each dotted side runs between two mirror copies of the same corner cell with period 2

reading: A partly drawn symmetric pattern is completed so that the output is symmetric about the grid's centre axes (both mirrors and the diagonal).
why: output equals the union of the input and its D4 images about the grid centre

reading: Every row and column of the solid block is extended in its direction (left, right, up, down) to the grid border in the block colour, except a row/column segment that contains a marker on that side, which is left empty (the marker stays).

slots.lines: each row and column of the block, per side, to the border
slots.blocker: an isolated marker cell lying on that line on that side; the whole line is then omitted

why: a ray from the block side is drawn to the border iff no marker lies on it

reading: Wherever four 2-cell bars (left, right, above, below) point at one background cell from distance 2, that centre cell is coloured 4.

new_rows.name: plus_centre
new_rows.datalog: plus_centre(Y, X) :- cell(Y, XA, C1), X = XA + 3, px(Y, X, B), !cell(Y, X, B), XB = X - 2, cell(Y, XB, C2), XC = X + 2, cell(Y, XC, C3), XD = X + 3, cell(Y, XD, C4), YA = Y - 3, cell(YA, X, C5), YB = Y - 2, cell(YB, X, C6), YC = Y + 2, cell(YC, X, C7), YD = Y + 3, cell(YD, X, C8).

why: exactly the cells with fg at offsets +-2 and +-3 along both row and column become 4

reading: Inside the 7 rectangle a line of 6s ends in a 2 head; a ray continues from the head in that direction through the 7s, and the first cell it reaches outside the rectangle (in the coloured frame) becomes 7. Nothing else changes.

slots.pointer: line of 6 ending at the 2 cell (direction 6 to 2, orthogonal or diagonal)
slots.path: 7 cells beyond the 2 along that direction
slots.hit: first non-7 cell on the path

why: exactly one cell changes: the first non-7 cell on the ray from the 2 away from the 6s

reading: Each 2 cell lying inside the bounding box of a 3 block gets a 3x3 ring of 1 around it (overwriting whatever is there, centre stays 2); 2s outside the blocks get nothing.

new_rows.name: inblock2
new_rows.datalog:
bminy(O, min(Y)) :- obj(O, Y, X), px(Y, X, C), C = 3.
bmaxy(O, max(Y)) :- obj(O, Y, X), px(Y, X, C), C = 3.
bminx(O, min(X)) :- obj(O, Y, X), px(Y, X, C), C = 3.
bmaxx(O, max(X)) :- obj(O, Y, X), px(Y, X, C), C = 3.
inblock2(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 2, bminy(O, A), bmaxy(O, B), bminx(O, D), bmaxx(O, E), Y >= A, Y <= B, X >= D, X <= E.

why: every changed cell is an 8-neighbour of an in-block 2 and becomes 1; in-block 2s remain 2
invariants: cells not adjacent to an anchor

reading: The grid is a lattice of identical small framed panels; when two panels in the same panel-row or panel-column carry the same unusual colour at the same inner position, every panel between them gets that colour at that position.

slots.lattice: equal panels separated by background lines
slots.position: a fixed offset inside a panel
slots.anomaly: colour at that offset differing from the majority over panels
slots.fill: panels strictly between two equal anomalies on one panel-row/column take that colour at that offset

why: for each offset, each panel-row and panel-column, the anomaly colour fills the span between its two occurrences

reading: The bottom row and right column are colour keys; each cell (y, x) whose right-column cell at row y and bottom-row cell at column x have the same colour c becomes c, giving a staircase of blocks along the anti-diagonal.

slots.cell_rule: cell (y,x) := c iff col_key[y] = row_key[x] = c

why: every changed cell has matching key colours in its row (right edge) and column (bottom edge)
invariants: cells with mismatched keys stay background

reading: The input is repeated twice side by side.
why: output is a 1x2 tiling of the input with both blocks filled

reading: The 3x3 input is tiled k by k, where k is the number of distinct colours in the input.

slots.extent: k x k blocks, all filled
slots.k: number of distinct colours in the input (2,2,4,3,3 in training)

why: output size is 3k x 3k and every block equals the input; neither pixel_count nor object_count gives k on all pairs
